text:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — using this thread for travel/offsite/workspace questions. I'll collect answers and pin the doc. @people-ops-bot please post the updated link when ready.

alex: Thanks! Two quick ones: 1) For domestic offsites, do senior ICs get flexible flight upgrades or still economy? 2) What's the guest/partner policy for multi-day offsites?

elaine: Great Qs. Short version: most company-paid flights are economy; upgrades aren't auto-approved — ask your manager & justify with itinerary conflicts or back-to-back meetings. Guests/partners: allowed for regional social offsites (e.g., local team get-togethers) but NOT for customer-facing or retreat-style events. We'll add examples to the doc. :memo:

jamal: If I want to work from a different city for a week (family reasons), do I need approval or just file something? Any tax/expense notes?

elaine: Please submit the "Remote Location Request" form at least 5 business days before travel. If you're crossing countries, talk to finance/legal first — there can be payroll/immigration implications. For US->US relocations <30 days it's usually fine; cross-border needs extra review.

people-ops-bot: Heads-up — Travel & Offsite Policy v2 uploaded: https://intranet.redwood/travel_offsite_v2 (edited)

alex: Thanks. And travel reimbursement: receipts only? Per diem?

elaine: Receipts required for flights, hotels, rides. We have a per diem for meals for domestic offsites: $65/day. For international, use the country-specific per diem in the doc. Expense snippet for Concur (copy/paste):

```
Expense type: Meals
Amount: 65
Date: 2026-04-14
Notes: Team offsite, SF hub
Receipt: attached
```

elaine: Also — if a manager pre-approves an upgrade (business class) due to schedule, please attach the manager's note in the expense.

sophie: Is there a coworking stipend or coverage for day passes when traveling to another city to be near a client?

elaine: Yes — eligible employees can opt into a $150/month coworking stipend. For short client trips, day passes under $25/day are reimbursable with receipts. Policy has opt-in steps; we'll publish a one-pager.

alex: What about car rental vs rideshare for offsites? For multi-person travel sometimes rental is cheaper.

elaine: Good point — rideshare preferred for single travelers under $75. Car rentals allowed for groups or when public transit isn't practical. Always include a short justification and split costs appropriately.

jamal: Any new guidance on office hoteling desks? I booked a hot desk at HQ but the calendar said reserved — how to handle?

elaine: We're rolling out a new hoteling flow next month to prevent double-books. For now, if you book and see a conflict, ping the desk-reservations channel and ops will reconcile. Policy: priority to scheduled meetings, then recurring desk owners, then one-off hoteling.

cto: One leadership note — for Dedicated on-prem visits, please clear security screening at least 48 hours in advance. No exceptions for late drop-ins.

alex: Clarify childcare/guest reimbursement? Are we covering daycare during official offsite days?

elaine: We don't reimburse routine childcare. For required travel where absence would prevent attendance (e.g., mandatory multi-day training), managers can request a childcare stipend case-by-case. Include receipts and manager approval.

maria: Appreciate the clear answers. I'll collate these into a short FAQ and pin it to the all-hands follow-up doc. If anyone needs 1:1 clarification, DM me or @elaine.

people-ops-bot: FAQ draft added to the all-hands folder: https://intranet.redwood/allhands/apr-2026/faqs

alex: awesome, thanks! :thumbsup:

elaine: Will update official policy doc by end of week with examples and a quick flowchart for approvals. If you want to volunteer to review language for clarity, lmk.

sophie: I can help review the coworking section.

maria: Perfect — tagging you in the draft.
